blocks.text: Victory is achieved by forcing enemy factions to surrender by controlling two critical resources:

items.text: Each territory has an MPC value that indicates:
How much income the controlling faction collects at the end of each turn
How many units can be produced there, or in an adjacent sea territory, each turn
MPC income can be spent to produce new units
Each scenario has an MPC multiplier (typically 2x) setting
Factions that fall behind economically, with a lower MPC total after applying the multiplier, can be forced to surrender
The special territories confer several benefits
Give bonus MPC
Units produced at SC have a lower cost
Each scenario has a minimum SC count per faction
Factions that fall below the minimum can be forced to surrender by another faction that controls one of their starting SCs

rows: Mustering: Can be deployed in contested territory, Dig In: +1 Defense when defending
Amphibious: Becomes a transport in sea spaces
Carrier Air Wing: Carry up to 3 air units
Submerge: Can’t engage or be attacked by aircraft
Bombardment: Can do 1 bombardment round against land as a Combat Move

items.text: Limited to 3 rounds
Roll attack die for each unit
Roll >= defense equals a hit
Deal damage equal to the damage rating
Target is chosen randomly from eligible units (Defense <= roll)
Units are twice as likely to hit the same unit type
Except bombers
Max number on the die always hits
If there’s no natural hit, the target is chosen from among the next lowest defense
If roll is < Defense
Deals half damage - rounded down
Typically 1
Recovering:
Damage persists. Units that have not engaged in combat for a full round recover at the end of the turn
Attacker rolls all attacks
Defending casualties are noted but not removed
Defender rolls all attacks
Attacking and defending casualties are removed
Capture territory if all enemies are removed and ground units remain
Surviving air units automatically return to their base or carrier after combat
Occurs even if the carrier made its own combat move
Attacking or defending fighters create a 1-round air superiority combat before main combat
Limited to air units
Units gain XP
1 XP for surviving a round of combat
1 XP for dealing damage in combat
5 XP grants a promotion
Increase in attack die size
Max of D12
+1 defense
Max of 10
+1 HP
Mechanical Infantry units can traverse water spaces
Become transports in marine spaces
Unit is destroyed with transport
Transports that survive a naval battle can continue a combat move into adjacent land
Territories being attacked by transported land units get a combat bonus in the first round of combat
No bonus if non-amphibious land troops are attacking
An attack with units remaining on both sides after the 3rd round of fighting will result in a contested territory
The territory still belongs to its original owner
It contributes to neither power's IPC total
Only infantry from the owning power can be mustered in the territory
Units can move out of the territory as a combat move
Can’t move into uncontested enemy territory
Units can move into a contested territory as a non-combat move
Units that receive a combat bonus receive:
Increase in attack die size
Max of D12
+1 defense
Max of 10
Combat bonuses are granted for the first round of a battle when:
Defender gets a bonus against amphibious attacks
Attacker gets a bonus when new sea units are deployed into a space they occupy
Owner of territory gets a bonus against formerly allied units on their territory after an ally withdraws from an alliance
